response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate * 1.0 / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day, COUNT(*) AS film_count FROM film WHERE rental_duration >= 5 GROUP BY rating), b AS (SELECT AVG(avg_rate_per_day) AS benchmark FROM g) SELECT g.rating, g.avg_rate_per_day, g.film_count, g.avg_rate_per_day / b.benchmark AS ratio_to_benchmark FROM g CROSS JOIN b WHERE b.benchmark IS NOT NULL

assumptions.assumption: A long rental period means rental_duration >= 5, so the cutoff value of 5 days counts as long.
The benchmark is the unweighted mean of the per-rating averages over the long-rental films only (the same filtered groups shown in the output), not over all films.
rental_rate is divided by rental_duration as a decimal (not integer) division, and the per-film values are averaged with AVG, which ignores NULLs.

alternatives.interpretation: Long rental means strictly more than 5 days (rental_duration > 5).
